text:
cuda-monitor-bot: ALERT • increasing ECC/page-retire events observed on gpu-pool4 (us-west-2). error velocity > threshold. tagging 3 cards for follow-up.

maria: saw this on the dashboard at 09:07 — small spike yesterday, steeper today. posting sample rates and device list.

sanjay: can you paste the metrics? which cards exactly?

maria: metrics snapshot (promql):
```
rate(gpu_memory_page_retire_total{pool="pool4"}[1h]) by (gpu_serial)
```
results: serials: GPU-5A2F, GPU-9C11, GPU-D03B. rates: 0.02 -> 0.11 -> 0.36 (per min) over last 24h.

kelly: who owns pool4? is this affecting any production routes?

maria: pool4 backs low-priority batch and some canary hosts. latency SLOs for hosted-api not impacted yet but we should act before a cascade. canary traffic is hit.

jamal: can we get nvml/Xid logs? also check page remap counters from the kernel. quick commands:
```
# nvlink/nvml
sudo nvidia-smi --query-gpu=serial,index,name,retired_page_count --format=csv
# kernel counters
sudo cat /sys/kernel/debug/gpu_remap/gpu-*/remap_count
```

maria: pasted outputs:
```
GPU-5A2F,0,A100,retired_pages=42
GPU-9C11,1,A100,retired_pages=71
GPU-D03B,2,A100,retired_pages=88
remap_count gpu-0: 420
remap_count gpu-1: 710
remap_count gpu-2: 880
```

sanjay: those remap_count numbers are high given the window. suggests progressive row remap rather than transient error. probability of full page retirement in next 48h is non-trivial.

kelly: agree. action plan?

maria: proposed: 1) cordon/drain GPU instances hosting canary routes; 2) move any critical workloads off pool4 to pool2 for 24h; 3) run extended memtest tool on the three cards; 4) open hardware RMA if memtest fails or remap counters still climb after soft reset.

jamal: add a step: pin a read-only snapshot of KV cache for jobs moved to pool2 so we don't warm incorrectly. also schedule a quick canary flood step after drain to validate no silent regressions.

sanjay: how long is drain estimated? we need capacity planning numbers.

maria: draining 3 hosts (~8 gpus total) with current autoscaler and preemptible batch means ~10-12 mins graceful shutdown + 20 min warmup on pool2. I'm provisioning 10% burst capacity from dedicated-reserve for 1 hour to avoid queuing.

kelly: cost hit for 1 hour is fine. please open infra ticket and tag hardware with serials so oncall/hw can follow RMA.

maria: opening ticket INF-3421: https://redwood.internal/infra/tickets/INF-3421 — includes logs, prom graphs, nvml outputs. tagging @sanjay @jamal for runbook.

cuda-monitor-bot: NOTE • automated escalation threshold reached. will continue to post hourly until remap rate drops below alert threshold or ticket closed.

jamal: quick triage checklist in ticket:
- run full memtest (48m) on affected cards
- attempt soft-reset via nvidia-smi --gpu-reset on idle hosts
- if remap_count growth persists after reset, mark for RMA and replace card
- update pool4 routing policy to prefer healthy pools for canaries

sanjay: also add a Grafana panel that shows remap_count slope (delta/hour) + retired_pages in same chart so we can detect velocity rather than absolute. set a 2x slope alert.

maria: doing that now. will post dashboards in INF-3421.

kelly: thanks — keep updates short here. if memtest fails, we do emergency replacement during maintenance window tonight. :thumbsup:

maria: update 09:41 — started drain on host pool4-host-12, moved 5 canaries to pool2, memtest scheduled on host-12 GPUs (run id memtest-176912).

jamal: ping when memtest completes. if it passes but remap_count keeps rising, we should still RMA — flaky remap behavior often precedes catastrophic failure.

maria: noted. will post pass/fail and next steps.

cuda-monitor-bot: UPDATE • 1hr check: GPU-9C11 remap_rate increased another 0.12/min over last hour.

maria: thanks — bumping priority in INF-3421 and marking for expedited memtest on 9C11.
